title: Generation Ghana Volunteer Programme 2026 | Become a Volunteer Mentor
summary: Generation Ghana is inviting professionals and experienced individuals to join its volunteer community and support young people as they transition from training into meaningful careers. Through mentoring, career guidance, and industry expertise, volunteers can help Ghana’s next generation of professionals build confidence, strengthen their employability, and prepare for the world of work. The programme is designed to create meaningful impact for learners while also giving volunteers an opportunity to develop their leadership, mentoring, and professional networks. About Generation Ghana Generation Ghana is part of Generation, a global organisation that works to transform education-to-employment systems by preparing, placing, and supporting people into careers that may otherwise be inaccessible to them. Through its programmes, Generation Ghana equips learners with practical technical and soft skills while providing the support they need to transition into employment. Why Become a Generation Ghana Volunteer? Volunteers are an important part of the Generation Ghana programme. By sharing your time, knowledge, and professional experience, you can help learners navigate the early stages of their careers. As a volunteer, you can: Support young professionals as they prepare for employment Share practical industry knowledge and career advice Help mentees build confidence and professional skills Develop your mentoring and leadership abilities Expand your professional network Gain meaningful volunteering experience Contribute to creating pathways to employment for young people in Ghana Volunteer Roles Available Generation Ghana offers three main volunteer opportunities. 1. Career Catalyst Coach Career Catalyst Coaches help graduates navigate the early stages of their job search. You may support mentees with: CV development Cover letter writing LinkedIn profile optimisation Interview preparation Job-search strategies Career-related guidance Your professional insights could help a graduate move from struggling with applications to successfully securing employment. 2. Sector Success Guide Sector Success Guides share their industry knowledge and professional experience with graduates entering the workforce. You can help mentees understand: Industry expectations Workplace culture Sector-specific skills Career pathways Professional standards What it takes to succeed in their chosen field This role is particularly valuable for graduates who need an insider s perspective on the professional world. 3. Personal Development Partner Personal Development Partners provide encouragement and guidance as mentees work towards their personal and professional goals. You can support learners in: Building confidence Setting achievable goals Developing self-belief Identifying their strengths Overcoming professional challenges Maintaining a growth mindset Sometimes, having someone who believes in your potential can make a significant difference. Volunteer Commitment Generation Ghana has designed the volunteering experience to be manageable alongside your professional and personal commitments. Volunteers are expected to: Attend a comprehensive onboarding training session Conduct 6 virtual mentoring sessions over 3 months Schedule sessions flexibly with mentees Complete brief feedback forms after sessions Complete an end-of-programme survey Total time commitment: Approximately 12–15 hours over 3 months. How the Generation Ghana Volunteer Journey Works Week 1: Application You begin by submitting the online volunteer application, including information about your background, interests, and availability. The Generation Ghana team reviews applications and sends successful applicants confirmation and information about the next steps. Week 2: Screening and Matching Selected applicants participate in a brief 30-minute interview to discuss their goals, expertise, and preferred mentoring approach. A background verification process is also conducted to support learner safety. Volunteers are then matched with 1–3 learners according to their professional experience and mentoring preferences. Week 3: Onboarding and Training Volunteers participate in a 2-hour virtual orientation and training session covering Generation Ghana s mission, learner profiles, and mentoring best practices. You will also receive a resource kit containing mentoring guides, session templates, and other support materials. A dedicated coordinator will be available to support you throughout the programme. Week 4: First Connection After being matched with a mentee, you will receive relevant background information and arrange your first session. The initial 60-minute session focuses on building rapport, setting expectations, and identifying the mentee s goals. Months 1–3: Active Mentoring Volunteers conduct five additional virtual sessions, usually on a bi-weekly basis or according to an agreed schedule. Throughout the programme, volunteers can access coordinator support and mentoring resources while remaining connected to the wider volunteer community. What Volunteers Say Generation Ghana s existing volunteer community highlights the value of sharing professional experience with emerging talent. Taronish Dastoor , Marketing Manager for Michael Page Middle East and Africa, described volunteering through digital marketing mock interviews as a rewarding opportunity to interact with motivated candidates and share practical career advice. Julien Raze , Managing Director of Middle East Africa at Page Group, highlighted the professionalism of the programme and encouraged professionals and organisations to contribute their time and expertise to employability initiatives. These experiences demonstrate that volunteering can benefit both the learner and the professional providing support. What Generation Ghana Learners Say Generation Ghana graduates have also highlighted the impact of mentorship, training, and career support. Learners have reported improvements in areas including: Communication skills Confidence Technical and soft skills Interview preparation Problem-solving Collaboration Professional mindset Practical workplace skills One Digital Customer Service graduate described Generation Ghana as an important source of support during their period of unemployment, particularly through interview simulations, preparation, facilitator support, and personalised guidance. Who Can Volunteer? The programme is particularly suitable for professionals and individuals who can share relevant career, industry, mentoring, coaching, or personal development experience. You can apply for one or more of the available volunteer roles: Career Catalyst Coach Sector Success Guide Personal Development Partner Previous mentoring or coaching experience is considered in the application, but applicants can indicate whether they have such experience. How to Apply Interested professionals can begin their volunteer journey by completing the Generation Ghana volunteer application form. Application: Apply to Become a Volunteer Mentor Applicants will be asked to provide their personal details, LinkedIn profile, mentoring or coaching experience, preferred volunteer role(s), and any questions or messages they may have. Final Thoughts Volunteering with Generation Ghana offers professionals an opportunity to turn their experience into practical support for emerging talent. With approximately 12–15 hours of commitment over three months , volunteers can contribute to career development while strengthening their own mentoring, leadership, and professional skills. If you have knowledge, experience, and a desire to help young people move closer to meaningful employment, becoming a Generation Ghana volunteer mentor could be a valuable way to make an impact. title: 2027 Mohamed Ali Foundation Fellowship at Durham University
summary: The Mohamed Ali Foundation is inviting applications for its 2027 Fellowship Programme , hosted at Durham University, UK . The fellowship supports scholars undertaking research on the Abbas Hilmi II Papers , a significant archival collection relating to the reign of Khedive Abbas Hilmi II and an important period in Egyptian history and East-West relations. The 2027 fellowship is particularly suited to early-career postdoctoral researchers and established scholars whose research connects with the themes identified by the fellowship s Advisory Panel. About the Mohamed Ali Foundation Fellowship The Mohamed Ali Foundation Fellowship Programme was established to encourage scholarly research into the Abbas Hilmi II Papers held at Durham University and to make the collection more widely known to researchers. The programme began in 2019 and is based at Durham University, where it is jointly tenable in the Institute for Middle Eastern and Islamic Studies (IMEIS) and Grey College . Fellows will conduct research on an agreed topic using the Abbas Hilmi II Papers and will deliver a lecture at Durham University. Their research will ultimately contribute to a volume of original scholarship, while lectures are also published through Durham University s Middle East Papers series. Research Areas for the 2027 Fellowship For the final year of the fellowship programme , the Advisory Panel is particularly interested in applications addressing the following areas: Infrastructure in its social and political context The use of new technologies to promote and publicise the Khedive to a wide audience Gender dynamics within the Khedival family and Egyptian society during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries The Khedive s estate and holdings , particularly their management through mechanisms such as waqf The nationalist movement and its relationship with the Khedive Political activism , particularly secret organisations and the use of methods such as assassination as political protest Applicants may propose alternative research topics, provided they are well grounded in the Abbas Hilmi II Papers and supported by their application proposal. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is open to: Early-career postdoctoral scholars Established scholars Applicants should note that making full use of the collection will often require good reading knowledge of: Arabic Ottoman Turkish French English Applicants are encouraged to familiarise themselves with the online catalogue of the Abbas Hilmi II Papers before preparing their proposal. Fellowship Location and Research Access The fellowship is based at Durham University and provides fellows with access to departmental and university facilities, including the University Library and Computing and Information Services. The fellowship normally provides accommodation at Durham during the Easter Term, from April to June 2027 . However, there is flexibility to arrange residency during different terms according to the fellow s availability. In some circumstances, fellows may be permitted to conduct their fellowship from Cairo or Istanbul , making use of the digitised collection, which is freely accessible online. All fellows are expected to visit Durham, at least briefly, to deliver their fellowship lecture in June. Fellowship Support Fellows who reside at Durham will be encouraged to participate in the University s academic and collegiate life, including seminars and other scholarly activities. The fellowship provides: An honorarium upon completion of the fellowship Accommodation for the duration of the fellowship All meals during the fellowship A research travel grant Access to Durham University facilities and academic resources What Applicants Need to Submit Applicants must complete both stages of the application process. Stage 1: Complete the Application Form Applicants must complete the official Mohamed Ali Foundation Fellowship Application Form . Stage 2: Submit Supporting Documents Applicants must send: A 2–3 page Project Proposal A Curriculum Vitae (CV) These documents should be sent to: maf.fellow@durham.ac.uk Applicants must complete both stages for their application to be considered. Application Deadline 📅 Deadline: Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Applications must be received by the deadline. For enquiries regarding the fellowship, applicants can contact: 📧 maf.fellow@durham.ac.uk How to Apply Interested researchers should review the fellowship information, familiarise themselves with the Abbas Hilmi II Papers , and prepare a research proposal that demonstrates how their project will make meaningful use of the collection. APPLICATION FORM Applicants can find additional information about the fellowship programme and application process on the Durham University fellowship page . Conclusion The 2027 Mohamed Ali Foundation Fellowship offers researchers an opportunity to undertake focused archival research into the Abbas Hilmi II Papers while engaging with Durham University s academic community. With the programme entering its final year, researchers whose work aligns with the identified themes are encouraged to carefully review the collection and prepare a well-grounded proposal before the October 20, 2026 deadline. title: Become a ONE Canada Global Activist: 2026–2027 Opportunity for Canadians Passionate About Africa, Global Health and Social Justice.
summary: The ONE Campaign is inviting passionate individuals in Canada to apply for the ONE Canada Global Activists 2026–2027 cohort . This volunteer opportunity is designed for people who want to advocate for stronger investments that create economic opportunities, improve health outcomes and support a healthier future across Africa. The program offers participants the chance to strengthen their advocacy, communications and leadership skills while becoming part of a wider international network of activists working to advance global justice. Applications for the 2026–2027 cohort are open to eligible residents of Canada, with the program scheduled to run from October 2026 to October 2027 . About the ONE Canada Global Activists Program The ONE Global Activists program brings together people who are passionate about tackling global inequality and advocating for policies and investments that can improve lives, particularly across Africa. As a Global Activist in Canada, participants will have opportunities to learn about advocacy, Canadian and international politics, development finance and media engagement. They will also be supported in taking meaningful action within their communities and engaging decision-makers on issues connected to ONE s advocacy priorities. The program is particularly suited to individuals who want to turn their interest in global development into practical advocacy experience. What Will Global Activists Do? Selected participants will become part of a network of advocates working to support ONE s campaigns and public advocacy efforts. Depending on their interests and activities, Global Activists may have opportunities to: Participate in advocacy campaigns focused on global development and Africa. Engage with elected officials and other decision-makers. Represent ONE at relevant events and activities. Take part in community-based advocacy actions. Help raise awareness of issues affecting global development and economic opportunity. Use communications and social media to mobilize people around advocacy campaigns. Connect with other activists in Canada and the wider ONE Global Activists network. Contribute creative ideas and actions that support ONE s advocacy priorities. The program therefore combines learning, networking and practical advocacy experience rather than being limited to classroom-style training. APPLY HERE. Training and Skills Development One of the major benefits of joining the ONE Canada Global Activists program is access to training designed to help participants become more effective advocates. Training will cover areas such as: Advocacy Participants can develop practical knowledge of how advocacy campaigns are designed and implemented, including how individuals and communities can influence public policy. Canadian and Global Politics The program provides opportunities to better understand Canadian politics and the broader international political environment in which global development decisions are made. Media and Communications Activists can strengthen their ability to communicate important issues through media, public speaking, social media and other communication channels. Development Finance Participants interested in international development can develop a stronger understanding of development finance and the investments required to support economic opportunities and healthier lives in Africa. These skills can be useful for individuals interested in communications, international development, nonprofit work, advocacy, public policy, community organizing and social impact. Networking Opportunities Joining the program also means becoming part of a broader community. Global Activists in Canada will have the opportunity to connect with other activists across Canada as well as members of the ONE Global Activists network in: Canada Europe Africa The United States This international network can provide opportunities to exchange ideas, learn from other advocates and build connections with people working on similar global issues. Opportunities to Meet Elected Officials Participants may have opportunities to represent ONE and engage directly with elected officials. This can provide valuable practical exposure to political advocacy and help participants understand how campaign messages can be communicated to policymakers. For people interested in public policy, government relations, international development, communications or political advocacy, this can be an important learning experience. Community Action and Advocacy Support Global Activists will receive dedicated support to develop and carry out creative community actions that contribute to ONE s advocacy work. This means participants are not expected to work completely independently. The program provides support as activists develop activities designed to raise awareness, engage communities and encourage action around important global issues. Key ONE Campaign Issues Applicants are asked to identify the ONE Campaign issues they are most passionate about. These include: Foreign Assistance Advocacy around international assistance and the investments needed to support development and reduce inequality. Global Health This includes issues such as: Vaccines Ending malaria Tuberculosis HIV/AIDS Strengthening global health systems Partnerships Between Canada and Africa Applicants can express an interest in strengthening relationships and partnerships between Canada and African countries. Energy Partnerships With Africa The program also welcomes people interested in creating stronger energy partnerships with Africa. Sharing African Stories Participants can also focus on communicating African stories and perspectives and helping ensure that African experiences receive greater visibility in public conversations. Applicants may also identify another area of interest if it does not fall directly within the listed categories. Who Should Apply? The program is intended for people who are passionate about global justice and interested in taking action on issues affecting Africa and international development. People with experience or training in areas such as the following may find the opportunity particularly relevant: Public speaking Social media Event planning Writing, including blogs and opinion articles Grassroots organizing Political campaigns Legislation and budgets Advocacy Community engagement Communications However, applicants are not restricted to people with experience in every one of these areas. The application allows individuals to identify the areas where they have relevant training, education or experience and to indicate areas where they would like additional training. For more information visit HERE. Leadership Experience Applicants are also asked about leadership positions they currently hold or have previously held in other organizations. This gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate their involvement in organizations, communities, campaigns, volunteer activities or other initiatives where they have taken responsibility or helped lead others. Commitment Required The ONE Canada Global Activist program requires participants to dedicate a few hours each month to the program. There may also be occasional requirements to attend: In-person events Trainings Advocacy activities Other program-related activities Applicants must therefore be able to commit to participating between October 2026 and October 2027 . Before applying, prospective applicants should consider whether they can realistically maintain this commitment alongside school, employment, volunteering or other responsibilities. Important Eligibility Requirement One of the most important conditions for this opportunity is that applicants must be residents of Canada . The application form specifically requires applicants to confirm that they are residents of Canada. Therefore, although the program focuses significantly on issues affecting Africa and welcomes people interested in partnerships between Canada and Africa, being based in Canada is a requirement for participation . People living outside Canada, including applicants currently residing in other African countries, cannot qualify for this particular Canada-based cohort simply because they are interested in African development. Age Requirement The ONE Canada Global Activist program is open to all ages , while placing particular focus on youth. The application asks applicants whether they are 35 years old or younger . This means the program is not presented as an opportunity exclusively for people under 35, but younger applicants are an important target group. African Diaspora Participation Applicants will also be asked whether they are members of the African diaspora . This question is included as part of the application and allows ONE to understand the backgrounds and communities represented among applicants. However, the application information does not state that being part of the African diaspora is a requirement for applying. The central geographic eligibility condition is Canadian residency. Previous ONE Global Activists Applicants are asked whether they have previously participated as a ONE Global Activist in Canada during either the: 2024–2025 cohort; or 2025–2026 cohort. This indicates that the application is designed to identify both new applicants and individuals who may have previously participated in the program. Program Period Successful participants are expected to commit to the program for approximately one year. The stated program period is: October 2026 – October 2027 Applicants should therefore be prepared to participate throughout this period and meet the program s monthly time commitment. Application Deadline The deadline to complete the application is: August 31, 2026 Applicants should complete the entire application form before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. Before submitting, applicants should make sure that all required personal information and application questions have been completed accurately. Information to Prepare Before Applying Applicants should be prepared to provide information including: Preferred pronouns First and last name Email address Phone number City Region Postal code Country Current occupation Whether they are part of the African diaspora Whether they are 35 or younger Previous participation in the ONE Global Activists program ONE campaign issues they are passionate about Their motivation for joining the program Areas of training, education or experience Other organizations they are involved with Their ability to commit between October 2026 and October 2027 Current or previous leadership roles Areas where they would like additional training Applicants should think carefully about their motivation and experience before beginning the application because several questions require written responses. How to Strengthen Your Application Applicants can improve the quality of their application by clearly connecting their interests and experience to the goals of the program. 1. Explain Your Motivation Clearly When answering why you want to become a Global Activist, avoid giving a generic response. Instead, explain what specifically motivates you to work on issues such as global health, Africa-Canada partnerships, foreign assistance, energy partnerships or sharing African stories. 2. Highlight Relevant Experience Think broadly about your experience. Relevant experience could include: Volunteering Student leadership Community projects Social media campaigns Writing Public speaking Event organization Advocacy Youth initiatives Nonprofit activities Political or civic engagement 3. Show Your Interest in Advocacy The program is specifically designed around advocacy, so applicants should demonstrate that they are interested in creating change and engaging people around important issues. 4. Be Specific About Training Needs The application asks whether there are specific areas where you would like to receive training. Use this question to identify genuine areas where developing additional skills would help you become a stronger advocate. 5. Demonstrate Your Ability to Commit Because the program runs from October 2026 to October 2027 and requires a few hours each month, applicants should demonstrate that they understand the commitment and can participate consistently. Application Process Interested individuals should first review the official ONE Canada Global Activist information sheet and Frequently Asked Questions before completing the application. The application is completed online and requires applicants to answer questions about their interests, experience, leadership background, availability and motivation. Applicants must confirm that they are residents of Canada. The application must be completed by August 31, 2026 . Privacy and Communications As part of the application process, applicants are provided with privacy information concerning how their information is handled. The form also gives applicants the option of signing up for communications from ONE about opportunities to take action on global inequality and related issues. Applicants can choose whether they want to receive these communications. The application also notes that submitting the form involves agreement to ONE s privacy policy, including provisions concerning the transfer of information to ONE.org s servers in the United States. Why This Opportunity Matters The ONE Canada Global Activist program provides an opportunity to move beyond simply learning about global development issues and become involved in advocacy. For participants, the program can provide a combination of: Advocacy training Political and policy knowledge Communications experience Media skills Networking Community engagement Leadership development Opportunities to interact with elected officials Exposure to international development and development finance Participation in a global activist network The experience may be particularly valuable for people interested in careers or future opportunities involving international development, nonprofit organizations, communications, public policy, advocacy, government relations and social impact. Final Thoughts The ONE Canada Global Activists 2026–2027 program is an opportunity for people in Canada who want to become more active in advocating for global justice, stronger Canada-Africa partnerships and investments that support economic opportunities and healthier lives in Africa. Participants can gain practical advocacy and communications skills, connect with activists across Canada and internationally, engage with elected officials and receive support for community-based actions. The program runs from October 2026 to October 2027 , requires a commitment of a few hours per month and may include occasional in-person events and training. Most importantly, prospective applicants should remember that Canadian residency is a mandatory eligibility requirement . If you are a Canadian resident who is passionate about Africa, global health, international development, advocacy or social justice, and you can commit to participating throughout the 2026–2027 program period, this could be a valuable opportunity to develop your advocacy skills while contributing to campaigns for global change. Application deadline: August 31, 2026. Official application: https://act.one.org/survey/global-activist-application-canada-2026/ Opportunity Category Category: Volunteer / Advocacy Leadership Program (ONE Global Activist program) Who Qualifies? Primary eligible group: Individuals who are residents of Canada . Age: The program is open to all ages, with a particular focus on youth. Applicants are asked whether they are 35 or under . Background: Applicants can come from different professional, educational and community backgrounds. Experience in public speaking, social media, event planning, writing, grassroots organizing, political campaigns, legislation/budgets or related areas can be relevant. Geographic eligibility: This specific ONE Canada program requires applicants to be resident in Canada . It is therefore not open to people applying solely from Kenya or other African countries while residing outside Canada. African diaspora: Applicants are asked whether they are members of the African diaspora, but the application information does not state that African-diaspora status is a requirement. Commitment: Successful applicants must be able to participate from October 2026 to October 2027 , dedicating a few hours per month and potentially attending occasional in-person events and training. Deadline August 31, 2026 Official Application https://act.one.org/survey/global-activist-application-canada-2026/ CLICK HERE for more OFY Fellowship opportunities. title: Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy at Google DeepMind: Apply for a Senior AI Governance and Policy Career Opportunity
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming economies, governments, industries, scientific research, and everyday life. As increasingly capable AI systems are developed and deployed, there is growing demand for professionals who understand how advanced AI can be governed responsibly while enabling innovation. Google DeepMind is seeking an experienced Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy to help shape governance frameworks, safety standards, regulatory approaches, government evaluation protocols, and external oversight mechanisms for frontier artificial intelligence systems. This is a senior-level opportunity for a professional with substantial experience in public policy, national security, AI governance, or the artificial intelligence industry , combined with specific experience in frontier AI safety and governance. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work from either London, United Kingdom, or Washington, D.C., United States , subject to the working-location arrangements associated with the position. Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy – Google DeepMind The Governance Manager will operate at the intersection of artificial intelligence, public policy, safety, security, regulation, international standards, and risk management . Google DeepMind describes AI as one of humanity s most transformative technologies and emphasizes the importance of developing advanced AI responsibly. The role is therefore designed for an experienced professional capable of helping translate emerging AI governance expectations into practical internal processes while also contributing to external standards and oversight frameworks. The position involves substantial engagement with governments, international standards organizations, industry coalitions, technical experts, auditors, and other stakeholders involved in the governance of advanced AI. Opportunity Details Organization: Google DeepMind Position: Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy Opportunity category: Job Career area: AI Governance, Public Policy, AI Safety and Security Work locations: London, United Kingdom; Washington, D.C., United States Level: Experienced/Senior professional Minimum education: Bachelor s degree or equivalent practical experience Minimum professional experience: 7 years in public policy, national security, or the AI industry Frontier AI experience: At least 3 years focused on frontier AI safety and governance Language: English proficiency is required unless otherwise stated United States compensation: $188,000–$205,000 USD plus a 15% target bonus Deadline: No specific application deadline is provided in the supplied vacancy information. Applicants should therefore check the official vacancy page and apply while the position remains open. What Is the Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy Role About? The role focuses on developing and influencing governance systems for increasingly capable AI models. As frontier AI systems become more powerful, organizations need effective mechanisms for assessing their risks, establishing technical and governance standards, responding to incidents, working with governments, and ensuring that safety practices are integrated into the development and deployment lifecycle. The Governance Manager will help address these challenges by connecting external developments in AI governance with Google s internal safety and security functions. This makes the position particularly relevant to professionals who have worked across areas such as: AI policy and regulation Frontier AI safety Technology governance National security Public policy AI risk management Technical standards Government relations Regulatory affairs AI auditing and assurance Incident disclosure frameworks International governance Responsible AI AI security Minimum Qualifications Applicants are expected to meet several core requirements before being considered for the position. 1. Bachelor s Degree or Equivalent Practical Experience Candidates must have a Bachelor s degree or equivalent practical experience . The vacancy does not restrict applicants to a particular undergraduate discipline. Relevant academic backgrounds may include fields such as public policy, international relations, political science, law, computer science, technology policy, national security, economics, engineering, or other disciplines connected to AI governance and policy. Equivalent practical experience may also be considered where applicable. 2. At Least Seven Years of Relevant Professional Experience Candidates need seven years of experience in public policy, national security, or within the AI industry . This requirement demonstrates that the role is intended for an established professional rather than an entry-level applicant. Relevant experience could potentially include work involving: Government policy Technology regulation National security policy AI industry strategy AI governance Public-sector technology policy Regulatory affairs International technology standards AI safety policy Government relations Risk and compliance Emerging technology policy Applicants should clearly demonstrate the connection between their previous work and the responsibilities of a frontier AI governance position. 3. Three Years Focused on Frontier AI Safety and Governance In addition to the broader seven-year experience requirement, applicants need at least three years of experience specifically focused on frontier AI safety and governance . This is an important distinction. General technology experience alone may not be sufficient. Candidates should be able to demonstrate meaningful professional involvement in questions surrounding the safety, governance, oversight, regulation, evaluation, or risk management of highly capable AI systems. Preferred Qualifications Google DeepMind also identifies several additional experiences that could strengthen an application. Experience Connecting AI Safety and Internal Risk Management Candidates with experience connecting AI safety best practices with internal risk management systems may be particularly well suited to the role. This could involve developing organizational processes that identify AI-related risks, establishing safeguards, coordinating risk assessments, or integrating safety requirements into product and technology decision-making. Experience With Third-Party Testing and Auditing Experience designing, negotiating, or managing third-party testing protocols, incident disclosure frameworks, or auditing regimes is another desirable qualification. This is significant because external evaluation and independent oversight can play an important role in establishing confidence in advanced AI systems. Candidates with experience working with external evaluators, auditors, testing organizations, regulators, or government assessment programs may therefore have relevant expertise. Experience Developing Technical and Governance Standards The organization is also interested in professionals who have a track record of drafting, negotiating, or influencing technical and governance standards . Applicants should emphasize occasions where they contributed to: Technical standards Governance frameworks Industry standards Regulatory frameworks Policy guidelines International agreements Risk-management standards AI safety protocols Where possible, candidates should explain their individual contribution and the outcome of the work rather than simply listing standards-related responsibilities. High-Trust International AI Safety Network Another preferred qualification is an established, high-trust network of global AI safety contacts . The vacancy specifically highlights relationships involving senior government officials, think tanks, and technical policy experts in major AI policy markets, particularly: United States United Kingdom European Union This suggests that stakeholder engagement and trusted relationships will be an important part of the position. Key Responsibilities The Governance Manager will have a broad range of responsibilities involving international standards, government evaluations, incident reporting, internal safety practices, and external oversight. 1. Engage With International Standards Bodies One of the responsibilities is engaging with international standards organizations such as ISO and INCITS , as well as industry coalitions including the Frontier Model Forum (FMF) . The objective is to contribute to the development of technical benchmarks and best practices for advanced AI. This means the successful candidate may participate in discussions about how frontier AI systems should be evaluated, governed, tested, and monitored. The role therefore requires someone who can understand complex technical and policy discussions and translate them into practical governance outcomes. 2. Establish Government Model-Evaluation Protocols The position involves establishing and overseeing steady-state protocols for unclassified and classified government model evaluations . Government evaluation of advanced AI systems can involve highly sensitive information and complex institutional requirements. The Governance Manager will therefore need to understand how evaluation frameworks can be structured and maintained while addressing security, confidentiality, safety, and governance considerations. 3. Develop Cross-Border Incident Disclosure Frameworks Another major responsibility involves negotiating frameworks for cross-border incident disclosure . As AI systems operate across jurisdictions, AI-related incidents may have implications for multiple countries and regulatory environments. The Governance Manager will help establish approaches for determining how relevant incidents are disclosed and coordinated internationally. This requires strong negotiation skills, knowledge of regulatory environments, and an understanding of how different jurisdictions approach AI safety and security. 4. Connect External Regulation With Internal AI Safety Teams The successful candidate will act as a bridge between external regulatory developments and internal safety and security teams . This is one of the central features of the position. AI regulations, standards, government policies, and industry expectations are continually evolving. The Governance Manager will need to understand these developments and translate them into practical internal processes. This may involve: Monitoring regulatory developments Interpreting emerging standards Advising internal stakeholders Coordinating with safety teams Supporting compliance planning Translating policy requirements into operational practices Helping inform AI system launch decisions 5. Shape External Oversight Policies The role also involves helping establish policies for external oversight of advanced AI systems . This includes defining: Auditor criteria Access protocols External evaluation requirements Oversight mechanisms Positions on regulatory regimes The successful candidate will therefore contribute to how external organizations and independent experts can assess advanced AI systems. Why This Google DeepMind Opportunity Is Significant The Governance Manager position is particularly significant because AI governance is becoming an increasingly important area of technology policy. Governments and international organizations are developing new approaches to the regulation and oversight of artificial intelligence. At the same time, AI companies are establishing internal safety frameworks and participating in international discussions about standards and responsible development. A professional in this position can therefore contribute to decisions that influence how frontier AI systems are evaluated and governed. The role combines several disciplines that are traditionally separate, including: Artificial intelligence Public policy National security International relations Technical standards Risk management Regulatory affairs AI safety Government engagement Corporate governance This makes it a particularly specialized career opportunity. Salary and Compensation For the United States location, the vacancy lists a compensation range of: $188,000 to $205,000 USD, plus a 15% target bonus. The exact compensation offered to an individual may depend on factors including job-related skills, professional experience, education, training, and other relevant considerations. The supplied vacancy information does not provide a separate salary figure for the London location. Google also provides employee benefits, with details available through its careers resources. Applicants should review the official employment terms and benefits information applicable to their selected working location. Work Locations Applicants are given the opportunity to indicate their preferred working location between: London, United Kingdom London is one of the world s major centers for technology policy, financial services, international organizations, government relations, and AI research. The location can be particularly relevant to professionals working across European AI regulation and international technology governance. Washington, D.C., United States Washington, D.C. is a major center for government, national security, public policy, technology regulation, and international affairs. The location may therefore be particularly relevant for professionals whose experience includes U.S. government policy, national security, AI regulation, or technology governance. Applicants should indicate their preferred location according to the arrangements specified in the vacancy. Who Should Apply? This opportunity is best suited to experienced professionals rather than recent graduates. Potential applicants may include professionals working in: AI governance AI safety policy Technology policy Public policy National security Government affairs Regulatory affairs AI risk management Responsible AI Technology standards International technology policy AI auditing and assurance Emerging technology governance AI industry policy Candidates should be able to demonstrate substantial professional experience and, importantly, specialized experience relating to frontier AI safety and governance. How to Strengthen Your Application Because this is a highly specialized senior position, applicants should avoid submitting a generic CV. 1. Highlight Frontier AI Experience Your CV should clearly identify your experience with frontier AI safety and governance. Do not simply state that you have worked in technology. Explain your specific involvement in AI safety, governance, regulation, evaluation, risk, or standards. 2. Demonstrate Policy Impact Where possible, quantify or explain the impact of your work. For example, identify: Policies you helped develop Standards you influenced Regulatory frameworks you contributed to Government stakeholders you engaged AI safety programs you helped establish Auditing or testing frameworks you managed International initiatives you supported 3. Emphasize Cross-Sector Collaboration The position requires interaction with governments, technical experts, industry groups, standards organizations, auditors, and internal teams. Your application should therefore demonstrate your ability to work effectively across sectors and disciplines. 4. Showcase Negotiation Skills Negotiation is particularly relevant to the responsibilities involving incident disclosure frameworks, standards, government evaluations, and external oversight. title: Micro-Learning on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards Based on SECAP: Free Online Course via WhatsApp
summary: The Micro-Learning on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards Based on SECAP is a free, self-guided online learning opportunity designed to help professionals and other interested learners understand how environmental, social and climate standards can contribute to sustainable, inclusive and resilient development. Delivered through WhatsApp , the micro-learning provides a flexible and mobile-friendly way to explore important sustainability concepts, practical tools and frameworks directly from a phone. Participants can learn at their own pace while engaging with short, focused learning content and an AI-supported chat bot About the Micro-Learning Course The course focuses on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards (ESC) inspired by SECAP 2021 . It addresses the growing need for sustainable practices in investment projects and inclusive development. title: GIZ South Africa Ideas Competition 2026: Funding for NPOs, CBOs and NGOs Creating Jobs Through the Just Energy Transition
summary: The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), through the Career Path Development for Employment (CPD4E) project, has announced an Ideas Competition for emerging and small nonprofit and community-based organizations in South Africa. The initiative seeks innovative project proposals capable of creating employment and income-generating opportunities for youth, women, and persons with disabilities within South Africa’s Just Energy Transition. The competition is particularly relevant for organizations working in skills development, employment creation, entrepreneurship, inclusion, renewable energy, green jobs, community development, and economic empowerment. Successful applicants will receive funding and capacity-building support to implement innovative and scalable solutions in designated Skills Development Zones in Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape . GIZ South Africa Ideas Competition 2026 at a Glance Opportunity: CPD4E Ideas Competition Implementing organization: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) Project: Career Path Development for Employment (CPD4E) Commissioned by: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) Co-funded by: European Union (EU) and Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) Implemented in partnership with: Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) Target applicants: Emerging and small NPOs, CBOs, NGOs and similar organizations Geographical focus: South Africa Focus areas: Employment, income generation, skills development and the Just Energy Transition Priority beneficiaries: Youth, women and persons with disabilities Target areas: Mpumalanga, Northern Cape and Eastern Cape Support: Funding and capacity-building Application deadline: 11 September 2026 at 5:00 PM SAST What Is the GIZ CPD4E Ideas Competition? The CPD4E Ideas Competition is designed to identify and support organizations with practical and innovative ideas for addressing employment and income-generation challenges associated with South Africa’s transition toward a more sustainable and inclusive energy economy. South Africa’s Just Energy Transition involves significant changes to the country’s energy and economic systems. While the transition toward cleaner energy can create new employment opportunities, it can also create challenges for communities and groups that need additional skills, resources, access to employment, and opportunities to participate in emerging industries. The competition therefore aims to identify solutions that can help people access economic opportunities connected to the transition. Applicants are encouraged to put forward ideas that are not only innovative but also capable of being implemented, expanded, and replicated in communities. What Is the Career Path Development for Employment Project? The Ideas Competition forms part of the Career Path Development for Employment (CPD4E) project. The project is commissioned by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-funded by the European Union and the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), and implemented by GIZ in partnership with South Africa’s Department of Higher Education and Training. The broader project is concerned with strengthening pathways toward employment and improving access to skills and economic opportunities. Through the Ideas Competition, the project seeks to work with organizations that understand local challenges and can develop solutions that respond directly to the needs of communities. What Is the Main Objective of the Competition? The central objective is to support innovative and scalable solutions that create employment and income opportunities within South Africa’s Just Energy Transition . Projects should demonstrate how an organization s idea can contribute to practical economic opportunities for people who may otherwise experience barriers to employment and participation in emerging sectors. The competition places particular emphasis on: Employment creation Income generation Skills development Economic inclusion Youth opportunities Women s economic participation Inclusion of persons with disabilities The Just Energy Transition Innovative approaches Scalable and sustainable solutions Who Are the Priority Beneficiaries? A major feature of the competition is its focus on groups that can face significant barriers when accessing employment and economic opportunities. Youth Projects may seek to help young people develop skills, access employment, establish businesses, participate in entrepreneurship, or enter emerging industries associated with the energy transition. Organizations with practical approaches to youth employment and skills development may therefore find this competition particularly relevant. Women The initiative also seeks to support solutions that improve employment and income opportunities for women. Potential projects could address barriers to women s participation in economic activities, entrepreneurship, skills development, or emerging opportunities linked to the Just Energy Transition. Persons With Disabilities Persons with disabilities are another priority group. Applicants may develop solutions that improve accessibility, skills development, employment pathways, entrepreneurship opportunities, or participation in economic activities for people with disabilities. Which Areas of South Africa Are Covered? The competition specifically identifies three Skills Development Zones: Mpumalanga Northern Cape Eastern Cape Applicants should therefore pay close attention to the geographical focus of the competition when developing their proposals. Projects intended for implementation within these areas should demonstrate an understanding of the local context and explain how the proposed intervention can contribute to employment and income opportunities. What Kind of Ideas Is GIZ Looking For? The competition is aimed at organizations with innovative ideas that can create jobs within South Africa s Just Energy Transition . The announcement does not limit applicants to one specific project model. This creates room for organizations to propose solutions that respond to particular local employment, skills, entrepreneurship, or economic-development challenges. Potential areas of relevance may include: Skills development linked to emerging green industries Employment pathways for young people Entrepreneurship and income-generation initiatives Women-focused economic empowerment Disability-inclusive employment models Community-based economic development Green skills and workforce preparation Career development initiatives Job matching and employment support Innovative approaches to vocational skills Small-business development Local economic opportunities connected to the energy transition Models that can be expanded or replicated in other communities Applicants should ensure that their actual proposal aligns with the official competition requirements rather than assuming that every project within these broad areas will automatically qualify. What Support Will Successful Applicants Receive? Successful applicants will receive two important forms of support. 1. Funding Selected organizations will receive funding to implement their proposed solutions. This funding is intended to help successful applicants move their ideas beyond the proposal stage and into practical implementation. Organizations should therefore demonstrate that their proposed activities are realistic and that the requested support can contribute meaningfully to achieving measurable results. 2. Capacity-Building Support In addition to financial support, successful applicants will receive capacity-building support . This is significant for emerging and small organizations because funding alone does not always guarantee successful project implementation. Capacity-building can help organizations strengthen their ability to plan, manage, implement, monitor, and potentially scale their interventions. Applicants should therefore consider how their organization can use both financial and non-financial support to strengthen the sustainability of their project. Why Is This Opportunity Important? The GIZ Ideas Competition provides an opportunity for smaller and emerging organizations to contribute to one of South Africa s major economic and development transitions. For communities affected by changes in the energy sector, the Just Energy Transition is not only an environmental issue. It also involves questions about jobs, skills, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, inclusion, and economic resilience. Organizations working directly with communities can often identify challenges that larger institutions may not see. Supporting these organizations can therefore help develop solutions that are grounded in local realities. The competition s focus on youth, women, and persons with disabilities also highlights the importance of ensuring that the benefits of economic transformation reach groups that may face barriers to participation. Why Should Organizations Apply? There are several potential advantages for eligible organizations. Financial Support Successful applicants will receive funding to implement their selected project ideas. Capacity Development Organizations will receive capacity-building support that can strengthen their institutional and project implementation capabilities. Opportunity to Test an Innovative Idea The competition provides organizations with an opportunity to turn an innovative concept into a practical intervention. Contribution to the Just Energy Transition Successful projects can contribute directly to creating employment and income opportunities within South Africa s transition toward a more sustainable energy economy. Focus on Underserved Groups Organizations can develop solutions that specifically address employment and economic opportunities for youth, women, and persons with disabilities. Potential for Scalability The competition specifically emphasizes innovative and scalable solutions , meaning applicants should think beyond a one-time activity and consider how their approach could potentially reach more people or be replicated elsewhere. What Makes a Strong Project Proposal? Organizations preparing an application should avoid presenting only a general idea. A strong proposal should clearly explain the problem, the proposed solution, the target beneficiaries, the implementation approach, and the expected results. Applicants should consider demonstrating: A Clearly Defined Problem Explain the employment, skills, income, or economic challenge that the project intends to address. An Innovative Solution Describe what makes the proposed approach different, practical, or more effective than existing approaches. Clear Beneficiaries Identify who will benefit from the project and explain how youth, women, and/or persons with disabilities will be reached. Local Relevance Explain the connection between the project and the relevant Skills Development Zone. Employment and Income Potential Clearly demonstrate how the project could contribute to employment creation, income generation, entrepreneurship, or improved access to economic opportunities. Feasibility Show that the organization has a realistic plan for implementing the proposed activities. Scalability Explain how the solution could potentially expand, reach additional beneficiaries, or be replicated in other locations. Sustainability Consider what will happen after the initial project support ends and how the intervention could continue producing benefits. How to Prepare Before Applying Organizations interested in participating should begin preparations well before the deadline. A useful preparation process can include: Review the official competition information carefully. Confirm that the organization meets the applicant requirements. Identify the specific employment or income challenge being addressed. Define the target beneficiaries. Develop a clear and innovative solution. Establish how the project connects to the Just Energy Transition. Determine how the project will operate in the relevant geographical area. Develop measurable objectives and expected results. Prepare a realistic implementation approach. Consider scalability and long-term sustainability. Gather the organizational information and supporting documents required by the official application process. Submit the proposal before the stated deadline. Important Deadline The closing date for the GIZ South Africa CPD4E Ideas Competition is: 11 September 2026 at 5:00 PM SAST. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their proposals. Organizations should allow sufficient time to review the requirements, develop their project concept, prepare supporting information, and complete the submission process. Who Can Apply? The competition is targeted at emerging and small NPOs, CBOs, NGOs and similar organizations . The opportunity is therefore designed for organizations rather than individual applicants seeking personal scholarships, internships, or employment. Eligible organizations should carefully review the official call for proposals to confirm the precise organizational eligibility criteria and any additional requirements before submitting an application. Countries and Continents Eligible to Apply This is a South Africa-focused opportunity . The announcement specifically refers to project implementation within Skills Development Zones in Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape . Therefore, organizations should not interpret the competition as a general worldwide funding opportunity. Organizations seeking to apply should verify the official call for proposals for the precise geographical and organizational eligibility requirements. The primary geographical focus is South Africa, Africa . APPLY HERE Who Is the Opportunity Best Suited For? The competition may be particularly suitable for small or emerging organizations working in areas such as: Youth employment Women s economic empowerment Disability inclusion Skills development Vocational training Entrepreneurship Community development Employment services Green jobs Renewable energy-related skills Economic empowerment Social innovation Just Energy Transition initiatives Income-generation programmes Organizations should, however, ensure that their proposed activities meet the specific requirements contained in the official call for proposals. Pro Tip for Applicants A strong application should do more than describe a good idea. It should demonstrate a clear connection between the problem, solution, beneficiaries, implementation plan, employment outcomes, and Just Energy Transition . Applicants should make it easy for reviewers to understand: What is the problem? → Who is affected? → What is the proposed solution? → How will it create jobs or income? → Why is the solution innovative? → How will it be implemented? → How can it be scaled? A proposal that clearly answers these questions can communicate its potential impact much more effectively. Implementation is led by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) in partnership with South Africa s Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) . The partnership brings together international development cooperation and South African institutional expertise to support employment and skills-related outcomes. Final Thoughts The GIZ South Africa CPD4E Ideas Competition represents an important opportunity for emerging and small nonprofit, community-based, and similar organizations with innovative ideas for creating employment and income opportunities within South Africa s Just Energy Transition. With funding and capacity-building support available to successful applicants, the competition can help organizations move promising ideas toward practical implementation. Its focus on youth, women, and persons with disabilities also makes inclusion a central component of the opportunity. Organizations operating in or connected to the targeted Skills Development Zones in Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape should carefully review the official call for proposals and develop applications that demonstrate innovation, feasibility, measurable employment or income outcomes, and potential for scalability.
